newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish BEST sets IPO minimum price at PLN 32.
newsitem.headline: Polish BEST sets IPO minimum price at PLN 32.

text.p: Polish trading and financial operations firm BEST PH SA has set the minimum price of its February public offering at 32 zlotys, the firm said in an abbreviated version of its issue prospectus.
The firm said the final price would be set by management and would be published no later than two days before the start of the subscription.
The firm is offering 500,000 existing shares and one million new shares, with up to 400,000 existing shares and up to 800,000 new shares offered in large-investor subscription on February 12-21.
From February 17 to February 28 small investors will be offered 200,000 new shares and 100,000 existing shares.
The company, based in the northern city of Sopot and employing 311, seeks a listing on Warsaw bourse's main market.
BEST made a net profit 3.1 million zlotys last year on sales of 34.3 million zlotys.
The prospectus said BEST expected to net 13.4 million zlotys, 23.3 million zlotys and 35.6 million zlotys in 1997, 1998 and 1999 respectively.
It said sales would rise to 48 million zlotys, 66.5 million zlotys and 90 million zlotys in those three years.
